official_text: No person shall drive a motor vehicle in any public place unless he holds an effective driving licence issued to him authorising him to drive the vehicle.
normalized_text: A driver must hold a valid, currently-effective driving licence that authorises the specific class of vehicle before driving it in any public place.

official_text: No owner of a motor vehicle shall permit the vehicle to be driven in any public place unless it has been registered in accordance with this Chapter and the certificate of registration has not been suspended or cancelled.
normalized_text: A vehicle cannot legally be driven in a public place unless it is registered and that registration is currently valid (not suspended or cancelled).

official_text: No person shall drive a motor vehicle in any public place at a speed exceeding the maximum speed, or lower than the minimum speed, fixed for that vehicle or class of vehicle under this Act.
normalized_text: Drivers must stay within the maximum and minimum speed limits set for their vehicle class; the enabling section itself does not set the numeric limits, which come from separate central/state notifications (see legal_sources: SRC_SPEEDLIMIT_SO1522E_2018).

official_text: Every person, above four years of age, driving or riding or being carried on a motorcycle of any class or description shall, while in a public place, wear protective headgear conforming to such standards as may be prescribed by the Central Government.
normalized_text: Riders and pillion passengers over age four on any motorcycle must wear a BIS-conforming helmet in public places; turban-wearing Sikhs are exempted.

official_text: No person shall use, except as a passenger, a motor vehicle in a public place, and no person shall cause or allow any other person to use a vehicle in a public place, unless there is in force a policy of insurance complying with the requirements of this Chapter.
normalized_text: Every motor vehicle used in a public place must be covered by a valid third-party insurance policy meeting statutory requirements, except where a specific exemption applies.

official_text: Whoever contravenes any provision of this Act, or of any rule, regulation or notification made thereunder, for which no other penalty is provided, shall be punishable for the first offence with a fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, and for a second or subsequent offence with a fine which may extend to one thousand five hundred rupees.
normalized_text: This is the residual/catch-all penalty clause: any violation of the Act or its rules that is not covered by a more specific penalty section is punished under this default fine schedule.

official_text: A person who drives a motor vehicle at a speed or in a manner dangerous to the public, having regard to all the circumstances, is punishable for a first offence with imprisonment up to one year and/or fine up to five thousand rupees, and for a subsequent offence within three years with imprisonment up to two years and/or fine up to ten thousand rupees.
normalized_text: Dangerous driving carries escalating imprisonment and fine exposure, with the harsher tier triggered by a repeat offence within a 3-year window.

official_text: A person who drives a motor vehicle while having, per a breath analyser test, more than 30 milligrams of alcohol per 100 millilitres of blood, or while under the influence of a drug to an extent that renders him incapable of exercising proper control, is punishable for a first offence with imprisonment up to six months and/or a fine of ten thousand rupees, with enhanced imprisonment and/or fine for a repeat offence within three years.
normalized_text: Indias legal blood-alcohol limit for driving is 0.03% (30 mg/100 ml); exceeding it, or driving while otherwise incapacitated by drugs, triggers escalating penalties on repeat offences.

official_text: Whoever drives a motor vehicle without wearing a safety belt, or carries passengers not wearing seat belts, shall be punishable with a fine of one thousand rupees.
normalized_text: Both the driver and passengers in a motor vehicle must wear seat belts; violation carries a flat fine, with a separate sub-clause covering unrestrained children under 14.

official_text: Whoever causes the death of a person by rash or negligent driving of a motor vehicle, not amounting to culpable homicide, and reports the accident to a police officer or Magistrate soon after the occurrence, shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine.
normalized_text: A driver who causes a fatal accident through rashness or negligence but reports it promptly faces a lighter maximum sentence (up to 5 years) than one who flees.

official_text: Where a driver causing death by rash or negligent driving escapes from the scene without reporting the accident to a police officer or Magistrate soon after the occurrence, the driver shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
normalized_text: Fleeing the scene of a fatal accident without reporting it carries a substantially harsher maximum sentence (up to 10 years) than staying and reporting. This subsection was carved out of the Sanhitas general 1 July 2024 commencement after nationwide transporter protests, and its own commencement date could not be confirmed as of this tables last verification.
